2. The set P = {x | x ∈ Z , –1< x < 1} is a
(1) Singleton set (2) Power set (3) Null set (4) Subset
steps: Integers strictly between −1 and 1 must be listed.
The only such integer is 0.
Therefore P={0}.
A singleton set contains exactly one element.
Choose option (1).

4. If B⊆ A then n(A∩B) is
(1) n(A–B) (2) n(B) (3) n(B – A) (4) n(A)
steps: B⊆A means every element of B also belongs to A.
The intersection contains exactly the elements common to both sets.
Because B is entirely inside A, A∩B=B.
Equal sets have the same number of elements.
Therefore n(A∩B)=n(B), option (2).

entries.question:
5. If A = {x, y, z} then the number of non- empty subsets of A is
(1) 8 (2) 5 (3) 6 (4) 7
steps: A contains three distinct elements.
Each element can either be included or excluded from a subset.
Hence the total number of subsets is 2³=8.
Exactly one of those subsets is empty.
Non-empty subsets =8−1=7, option (4).

entries.question:
6. Which of the following is correct?
(1) ∅ ⊆ {a, b} (2) ∅ ∈ {a, b} (3) {a} ∈ {a, b} (4) a ⊆ {a, b}
steps: The empty set is a subset of every set.
The elements of {a,b} are a and b, not the empty set.
The set {a} is a subset, but it is not listed as an element of {a,b}.
The symbol ⊆ compares sets, whereas a is an element here.
Only option (1), ∅⊆{a,b}, is correct.

7. If A∪B = A∩B, then
(1) A≠B (2) A = B (3) A ⊂ B (4) B ⊂ A
steps: Every element of A belongs to A∪B.
Since A∪B=A∩B, every element of A must also be in B.
Thus A⊆B; reversing the argument gives B⊆A.
Two sets contained in each other are equal.
Therefore A=B, option (2).

8. If B – A is B, then A∩B is
(1) A (2) B (3) U (4) ∅
steps: B−A consists of elements of B that do not belong to A.
The equality B−A=B means no element of B was removed.
So no element of B belongs to A.
The sets have no common elements.
Therefore A∩B=∅, option (4).

10. If n(A) = 10 and n(B) = 15, then the minimum and maximum number of elements in A ∩ B is
(1) 10,15 (2) 15,10 (3) 10,0 (4) 0,10
steps: The intersection cannot contain more elements than either set.
The smaller set A has 10 elements, so the maximum intersection size is 10.
That maximum occurs if A⊆B.
The minimum is 0 when A and B are disjoint.
Thus minimum 0 and maximum 10: option (4).

11. Let A = {∅} and B = P(A), then A∩B is
(1) { ∅, {∅} } (2) {∅} (3) ∅ (4) {0}
steps: A={∅} has exactly one element: the empty set.
Its power set contains its two subsets: ∅ and {∅}.
The element ∅ belongs to both A and B.
Therefore A∩B={∅}, option (2).

20. In a city, 40% people like only one fruit, 35% people like only two fruits, 20% people like all the three fruits. How many percentage of people do not like any one of the above three fruits?
(1) 5 (2) 8 (3) 10 (4) 15
steps: The groups liking exactly one, exactly two, and all three fruits are disjoint.
Their percentages are 40%, 35%, and 20%.
Together they account for 40+35+20=95%.
All people account for 100%.
The percentage liking none is 100−95=5%, option (1).
